tasks.title: Fix stage 3b's silent OCR-worker crash — tell "the worker died" apart from "the page had no text", and retry before degrading
tasks.doneWhen: Measured on this machine, gpu-test/wireframe.png, three back-to-back runs: two of them read 0 regions while reporting ocrAvailable true and the warning "OCR ran but found no text in the image." The worker had in fact exited 3221225477 (0xC0000005, ACCESS_VIOLATION) and SubprocessReader.ocr discarded the exit code inside a bare except. extract_text's own docstring requires "not read" and "read and found nothing" to stay distinguishable because the §12 degradation path depends on it; this restores that. SubprocessReader must inspect returncode and stderr, surface a worker-death warning distinct from the empty-page one, and retry a died worker before degrading. Degrading must still never raise (§12) and no confidence may be fabricated for an unread region (§10). The read rate over 10 consecutive runs on the reference wireframe is recorded in docs/EDGE-CASES.md — a fix whose effect on the crash rate is not measured is not evidence of anything.

tasks.title: Assign fusion slots from the OCR text before falling back to position
tasks.doneWhen: Measured on gpu-test/wireframe.png with stage 3b succeeding: OCR bound HEADLINE (0.99), LABEL (0.97), SUBMIT (0.92) and Image (0.86) to regions, and _slot_assignments' positional rule placed 0 of 7 texts in the correct slot — headlineSub took 'Image', heroImage took the bleed-through string 'eeneb', and ctaButton kept its template default while still reporting sourceOf 'wireframe'. Slot assignment must consult the text first: a keyword match claims its slot, the existing kind=='group' rule keeps statBadges, and position survives only as the fallback for what is left. Junk readings must be excluded by a confidence floor rather than by naming them. The reference set stays covered in full whatever the extraction contains (AGENTS.md rule 5), an unclaimed slot still carries null and not a fabricated number (§10), and the before/after slot-assignment score is recorded in docs/BENCHMARK-RESULTS.md as B-004.

tasks.title: Wire /perceive to the pipeline it already has — stages 2, 3a, 3b and 4 instead of the T-054 scaffold
tasks.doneWhen: Measured by calling POST /perceive with gpu-test/wireframe.png against the board at 100/100: every element came back sourceOf 'default' with bbox null, normalisation was the identity {scale 1.0, width null, height null}, confidence was null, and stages 2, 3 and 4 were all 'skipped' naming T-055/T-056/T-057 — tasks that are done, tested and unreachable from the endpoint. No task covered the seam: T-054 built the scaffold and T-058 owns the Node side, so the wiring belonged to nobody and a 100/100 board could not see it. /perceive must run normalise → detect_regions → extract_text → fuse and return what they produce: the real transform (§6 requires the normaliser to record it), real bboxes in normalised space, measured confidences and never fabricated ones (§10), and stage records carrying real status, timings and inline artifacts (§11.1, §11.2). Degradation stays supported rather than fatal: OCR absent or a dead worker is a 'degraded' stage and regions-without-text, not a 500, and an undecodable upload is still §12's 422 PARSE_FAILURE. Pinned by a test that feeds the reference wireframe through the endpoint and asserts sourceOf 'wireframe' on the elements a detection actually claimed.

None was visible on a board reading 100 of 100, because a task's files list covers a module and nothing owns the call from one module to the next — a dependency graph over tasks cannot express 'and something must invoke this'. AGENTS.md must carry the rule that closes the class: a task that builds a module either wires it into a caller or names the task that will, and a task whose only test imports its own subject has not shown the module is reachable. tasks.title: The seed inserts hardcoded IDs without advancing the allocator, so the first generated section duplicates every seeded ID
tasks.doneWhen: Root cause found, and it is not where T-109 left it. server/src/store/seed.js inserts the Pulse Fit section and elements from data/seed/*.json with hardcoded ids -- section 1000000001, elements 2000000001 through 2000000007, pageName Home -- and never advances the store's counters, which start at exactly 1000000001 and 2000000001. So the FIRST generated section is allocated the same sectionId and the same seven fieldIds as the seeded one. That violates rule 4 and §1 outright, and the pre-submit gate's duplicate-ID check exists for precisely this. It also explains T-109's symptom: adding §3's `pageName` to generated elements made them visible to hydrateElements, which filters on `el.pageName === pageName`, and the duplicate fieldIds then overwrote the seeded values in allSections.Home -- so a PATCH moved the seeded document while the render read the generated one, and the §9 assertion failed at step 4. The page-hydration path was never the defect. Done when the seed advances every counter past the highest id it inserts, using only the store adapter's existing interface so Mongo and JSON behave the same; when generate.js emits §3's `loop`, `projectName` and `pageName` and elementValidator runs at the insert path (the half T-109 deferred); when a test asserts a generated section shares no id with the seed; and when the §9 store-liveness assertion passes with all of it in place. The placeholder test `the element document is still missing §3's loop, projectName and pageName` must be replaced by its opposite, not deleted.
